summary: An Indologist and linguist, Dieter B. Kapp completed his Dr. phil. at Heidelberg University under Hermann Berger. He held positions at Heidelberg (1971–1987) and served as director of the Institut für Indologie und Tamilistik at the University of Cologne (1990–2006).

Working in Indology and history/archaeology, Dieter George held a post at the Royal Library of Berlin from around 1972 to 1985. From circa 1978 to 1985, he edited the series Verzeichnis der orientalischen Handschriften in Deutschland, succeeding Wolfgang Voigt.

Dieter Gunkel is a scholar in linguistics and Indology who studied at the University of California, Los Angeles (~2004–2010). He held academic posts at the University of Munich (2010–2017), the University of Richmond (2017–2024), and UCLA (2024).

Specializing in Indology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology, Dieter Schlingloff earned his doctorate at the University of Göttingen under Ernst Waldschmidt and his habilitation at Humboldt University. His academic posts included Kiel University (1968–1971) and the University of Munich (1972–1996).
Dieter Schrapel is an Indologist who completed his doctoral degree at the University of Marburg under the supervision of Wilhelm Rau, attested in 1970.

Dieter Schuh is a Tibetologist who studied at the University of Cologne and the University of Bonn, where he earned his PhD and Habilitation. He served as außerplanmäßiger Professor at Bonn (1978–2007) and directed the International Institute for Tibetan and Buddhist Studies.

Dietmar Rothermund was a historian and Indologist who studied at Marburg, Munich, and the University of Pennsylvania (PhD). He spent his career at Heidelberg University, serving as Wissenschaftlicher Assistent in 1963 and holding the Chair of South Asian History (1968–2001).

Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche was a Tibetan Buddhist master in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under teachers including Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Shechen Gyaltsap Gyurme Pema Namgyal, and succeeded Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje from 1987 to 1991.

Dilip K. Chakrabarti is a scholar of archaeology and Indology who studied at the University of Calcutta. He held teaching posts at the University of Calcutta (1965–1977), University of Delhi (1977–1990), and served as Professor of South Asian Archaeology at Cambridge (1990–2008).

Dilip Kumar Biswas worked in history/archaeology and Indology. He studied at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta, where he was a student of Prabodh Chandra Bagchi, and later held academic posts at Calcutta and Visva-Bharati University.

Dilli Raman Regmi was an Indologist and historian who earned an M.Litt from the University of Madras and a D.Litt. from Patna University (~1941–1961). He taught at Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith from circa 1945 to 1947.

Dina Bangdel was a scholar of history/archaeology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She held academic appointments at Ohio State University (~1999–2002) and Virginia Commonwealth University (~2002–2017).

Dines Andersen was a Danish Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Copenhagen under Vilhelm Thomsen, Karl Verner, and Michael Viggo Fausbøll. He served at Copenhagen University Library (~1883–1903) and as Professor at Copenhagen University (1903–1927).

Dineschandra Sircar was an Indologist and historian who served as Lecturer and Carmichael Professor at the University of Calcutta (1937, 1962). He also served as Government Epigraphist for India at the Archaeological Survey of India.

Ding-hwa Evelyn Hsieh is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who earned her PhD from the University of California, Los Angeles. In 1998, she was appointed professor of Philosophy and Religion at Truman State University.

Dipa Ma was a teacher in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under Mahasi Sayadaw and Anagarika Munindra between 1964 and 1967, and taught prominent meditation figures including Sharon Salzberg, Joseph Goldstein, Jack Kornfield, and Sylvia Boorstein.

Dipak Kumar Barua is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held appointments at the University of Calcutta as Assistant Lecturer in Pali (~1964–1974) and faculty Dean (1987), and later served as head of Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (~1996–2003).

Dipak Ranjan Das is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied under Dineschandra Sircar. He held posts at Sanskrit College and University (attested 1966) and the University of Calcutta (attested 1994).

Dipesh Chakrabarty is a historian and philosopher who earned a PhD from the Australian National University. He taught at the University of Melbourne (~1983–1995) and became the Lawrence A. Kimpton Distinguished Service Professor at the University of Chicago in 1995.

Dirk H. A. Kolff is an Indologist and historian who completed his MA and doctorate at Leiden University. He served at Leiden University as a lecturer in 1967 and held the Chair of Indian History from 1971 to 2003.
